rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps
rows.expected_answer: You choose the order and the best answer is 6. Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). Timestamps are irrelevant for replacement effects; that is the layer system for continuous effects.

outcome.answer:
Order it Scales first, then Season, and **Walking Ballista** enters with **6** +1/+1 counters. You pick the order. Timestamps don't matter.

The Ballista would enter with 2 counters. **Hardened Scales** and **Doubling Season** are both replacement effects trying to change that same event. Per `616.1`, the player affected chooses which one applies first. After that, `616.1f` repeats the process for whatever still applies. The Scales ruling says this directly: you choose the order "no matter who controls the sources of those effects." Both cards also apply to a creature entering with counters, not just to counters added later (see the rulings below).

Your two options:
- Scales first: 2 + 1 = 3, then Season doubles it to **6**.
- Season first: 2 × 2 = 4, then Scales adds one for **5**.

So apply Hardened Scales first and you get a 6/6 for {4}.

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

outcome.answer:
No. Under **Blood Moon** each Tron land is just a Mountain that taps for {R}. You get three red mana in total, not 7 colorless, and **Urza's Tower** can't tap for {C}{C}{C}.

Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains." The Urza's lands are nonbasic because they lack the basic supertype (305.8). This is a type-changing effect, applied in layer 4 (613.1d). Per 305.7, when an effect sets a land's subtype to a basic land type, the land loses "all abilities generated from its rules text, its old land types" and gains the matching basic land mana ability.

So Tower, Mine and Power Plant each:
- lose the printed "{T}: Add {C}. If you control…" ability
- lose their Urza's land types
- gain "{T}: Add {R}"

The Tron bonus is gone in two ways. The abilities that would grant it no longer exist. Even if they did, the Tron check "checks for land types, not the names", and those types have been overwritten. The lands keep their names, though; they just aren't named "Mountain".

If you remove Blood Moon, they're back to normal immediately and you'll have your 7 mana again.

Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's (613.8a): applying Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain and strips its rules-text ability (305.7), which removes the existence of Urborg's effect. When a dependency exists it overrides timestamps (613.8), so Blood Moon applies first no matter which entered later (613.8b). Your friend is right. With **Blood Moon** on the battlefield, **Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth** doesn't make anything a Swamp, and it doesn't matter which one came down first. Dependency decides this, not timestamps.

Both effects are type-changing effects in layer 4. Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains." Urborg is a nonbasic land, so it becomes a Mountain. A dependent effect waits until the effects it depends on have been applied (`613.8b`), and "If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system" (`613.8`). So Blood Moon applies first. By the time Urborg's turn would come, Urborg no longer has the ability, so its effect never applies. Urborg's later timestamp doesn't help.

The Scryfall ruling on Urborg says the same thing (it uses Magus of the Moon, which has the same effect): Urborg "won't turn lands into Swamps, no matter in what order those effects started to apply."

Result: Urborg is a legendary Mountain that only taps for {R}. Your other nonbasic lands are just Mountains. Basic lands keep their normal types.

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
Their **Clone** is a regular Tarmogoyf. It doesn't get your counters or the Giant Growth boost. It also works out its own size with no trouble, because it copies the ability that sets Goyf's power and toughness.

Per `707.2`, a copy takes only the copiable values, meaning what's printed on the card. That rule says "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." Clone's rulings say the same: it doesn't copy counters or "any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness". So your two +1/+1 counters and the +3/+3 from **Giant Growth** stay with your Goyf only.

The Clone does copy Goyf's rules text. Per `707.2a`, "A copy acquires the abilities of the object it’s copying because those values are derived from its rules text." So the Clone has "Tarmogoyf's power is equal to the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1." It counts the graveyards itself and will always be the same base size as your Goyf.

Example: say the graveyards hold a creature, a land and Giant Growth itself, which is an instant that went to the graveyard after it resolved. Base Goyf is then 3/4. Yours is 3/4 + 2 counters + 3/+3 = 8/9 until end of turn, and theirs is 3/4. Next turn yours is 5/6 and theirs is still 3/4 (if the graveyards haven't changed).

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer:
Your ordinary creatures are 1/1 with no abilities in either order. The order only changes the result for **Humility** itself and for any other non-Aura enchantments.

**Humility first, then Opalescence (your situation):** In layer 4 (613.1d), Opalescence makes Humility a creature. Opalescence "Does not animate itself," so it stays a non-creature enchantment and keeps its ability. In layer 6, Humility removes abilities from all creatures, including itself. Its effect still carries on into later layers, because per 613.6 it continues "even if the ability generating the effect is removed during this process." In layer 7b, both cards set base P/T (613.4b). Neither effect changes what the other applies to or does, so they don't depend on each other (613.8a), and timestamps decide the order (613.7, 613.7a). Humility's 1/1 applies first. Then Opalescence's later effect sets Humility to its mana value. Result: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. Opalescence is a plain enchantment. Your creatures are 1/1 with no abilities. Any other non-Aura enchantment is a creature with no abilities whose P/T equals its mana value.

**Opalescence first, then Humility:** Layers 4 and 6 work the same way. In 7b, though, Opalescence sets Humility to 4/4 first, and then Humility's later effect makes every creature 1/1. Result: Humility and every other animated enchantment are 1/1 with no abilities, your creatures are 1/1, and Opalescence is still not a creature.

If one of your creatures is also a non-Aura enchantment, it gets the same result as the enchantments above.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer:
Yes. You can cast **Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor** for {5}{B}{R}. Per `712.11b`, when you cast a modal double-faced card you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack. Only the face you cast is checked to see whether you can cast it (`712.11c`).

No, it's not a planeswalker card in your library or graveyard. Per `712.8a`, a double-faced card in any zone other than the battlefield or the stack has only its front face's characteristics. There it's just **Valki**, a legendary creature card with mana value 2. Tibalt's planeswalker characteristics only exist while that face is up on the stack or the battlefield (`712.8f`).

For the cards you named:
- **Vraska's Contempt** only ever targets permanents, so the graveyard question doesn't come up. If Tibalt is on the battlefield, it's a planeswalker and Contempt can exile it. If Valki is on the battlefield, it's a creature, so Contempt can exile that too.
- **Kaya's Ghostform** can enchant Tibalt while it's on the battlefield. When Tibalt dies or is exiled, Ghostform says to "return that card to the battlefield under your control." A double-faced card put onto the battlefield from anywhere other than the stack comes in front face up (`712.14`), so it comes back as Valki, not Tibalt. Valki's enters trigger then goes off.

rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? And separately, if I have two Ragavan on the battlefield somehow, when exactly does the legend rule kick in - can I respond in between?
rows.expected_answer: 1) It doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would receive priority, not in the middle of a spell resolving (704.3, 704.4 - the CR's own Maro example). The creature only dies if it still has toughness 0 or less when SBAs are next checked (704.5f). 2) The legend rule (704.5j) is also a state-based action: the moment a player would get priority with two Ragavans you control, you choose one and the other goes to the graveyard. It doesn't use the stack and there is no window to respond between the second Ragavan entering and the legend rule applying; you can only respond before the second one enters/resolves.

outcome.answer:
**First question:** no, it doesn't die, as long as its toughness is back above 0 by the time that other spell finishes resolving. **Second question:** no, you can't respond. The legend rule is applied before anyone gets priority.

**The 0-toughness moment:** The game only checks state-based actions when a player would get priority. At that point it checks for the listed conditions and performs all of them at once (`704.3`). Per `704.4`, state-based actions "pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability." A creature with 0 toughness only goes to the graveyard under `704.5f` if its toughness is still 0 or less when that check happens. The **Maro** ruling says the same: if toughness drops to 0 mid-resolution and comes back up before the resolution ends, "it won't be put into your graveyard." **Giant Growth** doesn't change any of this. The one thing that matters is the creature's toughness after the spell has completely finished resolving. If it's still 0 or less then, it dies at the next check.

**Two Ragavans:** Per `704.5j`, if you control two or more legendary permanents with the same name, you choose one to keep and the rest go to the graveyard. Per `704.1`, state-based actions don't use the stack, and per `117.2d` they're dealt with before a player would receive priority. So as soon as the second **Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer** is on the battlefield, the next check happens before you or anyone else gets priority. You choose which one to keep, the other goes to the graveyard, and only then does anyone get priority. There's no window to act while you control both.

rows.question: I attack with a 5/5 trample that also has deathtouch (Questing Beast) and they block with a 4/4. how much can I trample over? my opponent says I have to assign 4 to the blocker first

A good answer says so. For the creature the asker describes, a 5/5 with trample and deathtouch, you only need to assign 1 damage to the 4/4 and can trample 4 over to the player. The 4/4 is then destroyed by deathtouch as an SBA.

outcome.answer:
Your opponent is wrong here. With deathtouch and trample, 1 damage on the 4/4 counts as lethal, so you can assign 1 to the blocker and trample the other 4 over. You can also put more on the blocker if you want to.

Per `702.19b`, a trampler has to assign lethal damage to its blockers before any excess can go to the player. That doesn't mean damage equal to the blocker's toughness. Per `702.2c`, "any nonzero amount of combat damage assigned to a creature by a source with deathtouch is considered to be lethal damage." So 1 damage satisfies the requirement and the remaining 4 can go to the player.

rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?
rows.expected_answer: 1) Yes. Color identity includes mana symbols in the mana cost AND in the rules text (903.4), so Kenrith's identity is WUBRG even though his mana cost is only {4}{W}. Nicol Bolas, the Ravager (UBR) is legal because every color in its identity is in Kenrith's (903.5c). 2) Yes, Kenrith can go to the command zone. If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead - a replacement effect (903.9b). Graveyard/exile use a separate state-based action (903.9a). Either way it's optional.

outcome.answer:
1) **Yes**, you can run it. 2) **Yes**, you get the choice: Kenrith can go to the command zone instead of your hand.

**Deck building:** Per `903.4`, a card's color identity is the colors of the mana symbols in its mana cost *and* its rules text. Kenrith costs {4}{W}, and his abilities use {R}, {G}, {U} and {B}, so his identity is all five colors. **Nicol Bolas, the Ravager** costs {1}{U}{B}{R}. Its back face also counts per `903.4d`, and that face's color indicator makes it blue, black and red. So Bolas's identity is blue, black and red. Every one of those colors is in Kenrith's identity, which is all `903.5c` requires.

**Unsummon:** **Unsummon** says "Return target creature to its owner's hand." `903.9b` covers this: "If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead." This is a replacement effect, so you decide as Unsummon resolves. Kenrith either goes straight to the command zone or goes to your hand, whichever you choose. It's optional, so you can keep him in hand if you'd rather cast him from there. The graveyard/exile option you're thinking of is a separate rule, `903.9a`, and it works as a state-based action. Hand and library are handled by the replacement in `903.9b`.

rows.question: commander damage question. I've been hit for 15 by my opponent's Rafiq. she then copies it with a Clone and hits me for 6 more with the clone. do I lose? also does the 21 count noncombat damage like from Fling?
rows.expected_answer: No to both. A player loses when they've been dealt 21 or more COMBAT damage by the SAME commander over the course of the game (903.10a; checked as a state-based action, 704.6c). The Clone copying Rafiq is not a commander, so its 6 damage isn't commander damage - you're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. Fling damage is noncombat, so it never counts toward the 21 either; it just reduces your life total normally.

outcome.answer:
No, you don't lose to commander damage. The 6 from the **Clone** doesn't count toward Rafiq's 21, and Fling damage never counts.

**Clone:** Being a commander belongs to the physical card. It isn't something a copy can pick up. Per `903.3`, the designation "is not a characteristic of the object represented by the card", and the rule's own example says a permanent that's copying a commander is not a commander. A Clone copying **Rafiq of the Many** is just a creature with Rafiq's text. `903.10a` only counts combat damage "by the same commander". You're at 15 from the real Rafiq and 0 from anything else. Once that real card has dealt you 6 more combat damage, you lose.

**Fling:** No. `903.10a` only counts combat damage. **Fling**'s damage is noncombat. It's also dealt by Fling itself, not by the commander: "Fling deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to any target." Even if she sacrifices Rafiq to Fling, that damage doesn't add to the 21.

All of that damage still comes off your life total as normal (`119.2`). Starting from 40, the 15 + 6 puts you at 19 if nothing else has changed it.

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?
rows.expected_answer: 1) No. Each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana added during your upkeep is lost before your main phase (106.4). Tap the lands in your main phase instead. 2) Yes. Casting a spell includes a step where, if the total cost includes mana, you get a chance to activate mana abilities such as tapping lands (601.2g), and only then do you pay the total cost (601.2h). You do not need to float mana before announcing the spell.

outcome.answer:
1) No. The mana disappears at the end of your upkeep. Mana pools empty at the end of every step and phase, and upkeep is a step of the beginning phase (`501.1`). Per `106.4`, "Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, and the player is said to lose this mana." Your lands would also stay tapped until your next untap step, so tapping them in upkeep only cuts you off from the mana you need for **Jace, the Mind Sculptor**. Tap them in your main phase as you cast him.

2) You can tap lands in the middle of casting **Snapcaster Mage**, and you don't need to float mana first. Per `601.2g`, once the total cost is set, "If the total cost includes a mana payment, the player then has a chance to activate mana abilities". Then you pay at `601.2h`. `605.3a` also lets you activate mana abilities "whenever they are casting a spell or activating an ability that requires a mana payment". The normal way is to announce the spell, tap your lands, and pay. Mana abilities don't use the stack (`605.3b`), so nobody can respond between tapping and paying.

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
rows.expected_answer: No copy. Academy Manufactor's "instead" makes it a replacement effect (614.1a), and Shelob's trigger would create a Food token, so Manufactor applies. The replaced event never happens (614.6): instead of the Food that would be a copy of the creature, you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure token. Those are predefined tokens with only their standard characteristics (111.10a, 111.10b, 111.10f). 111.10 lets the effect that creates a predefined token modify it, but Shelob's modifications belonged to the replaced event, and Manufactor's own effect modifies nothing. You end up with a plain Food, a plain Clue and a plain Treasure, and the creature is not copied.

outcome.answer:
You don't get the copy. **Academy Manufactor** replaces the creation of Shelob's Food copy, so you end up with one plain Food, one plain Clue and one plain Treasure, and no copy of the creature.

The token **Shelob, Child of Ungoliant** would create is a Food ("it's a Food artifact"), so it counts as a Food token for Manufactor: "If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each." That is a replacement effect (`614.1a`). Once an event is replaced, it never happens, and the modified event happens instead (`614.6`). So the Food copy is never created. The "one of each" you get instead are new, predefined tokens: a Food is "a colorless Food artifact token with “{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life.”" (`111.10b`), a Clue is defined by `111.10f` and a Treasure by `111.10a`. The copy characteristics came from Shelob's effect, and that effect is the event that got replaced, so none of the three new tokens is a copy of the dead creature. This means none of its ETB triggers happen either.

If you'd rather have the copy, you'd need Manufactor off the battlefield when Shelob's trigger resolves.
